manifest.binary: crates/sparkles-owl/examples/el_classify.rs and the sparkles CLI, built with mbx build --release on stanley at 6ae55297, whose sparkles-owl and sparkles-server sources equal 1e0760c9, and copied to the benchmark host
manifest.lock_note: Each run took ~/lanes/.bench.lock and ~/lanes/.heavy.lock for itself, and env.txt gives the time and the load average when it took them. Other lanes' benchmark jobs ran between the runs and never beside them, so the load averages at the lock include their tail.

reference.harness: ElkClassify.java sha256 5f879733... and konclude.py sha256 42eb3da4... of commit ea96e8f5, built into the packages on stanley and copied to forge's store with nix copy
reference.java: OpenJDK 17.0.20.1 from nixpkgs, named by each package's wrapper

method: run.sh.txt ran one process per tool, ontology and thread count. el_classify's classifyMs holds each classification of a fresh classifier with the axioms in memory and readMs the parse. ElkClassify's classifyMs runs from the creation of the reasoner to the end of precomputeInferences with a fresh OWL API manager and reasoner each run, and loadMs holds the OWL API's load. Konclude ran one process per classification. Its classifyMs is the total processing time of its log minus its parse time, so it includes the writing of the class hierarchy, and wallMs is the whole process. The end-to-end rows of robot.jsonl time robot reason --reasoner ELK and sparkles ontology classify --format ofn from the release's RDF/XML file to the written functional-style file, with timed.py.txt. oracle/ compares each reference taxonomy with the classifier's on one thread, and robot-reason with el-oracle.py --asserted. ours-threads.txt compares the classifier's taxonomies on one and eight threads.
scale: GO 2026-07-26, ChEBI lite 256 and the 8 ORE 2015 EL ontologies with the most classes

heap.elk: 4g on GO and ChEBI lite, 8g on ORE
heap.hermit: 8g on GO and ChEBI lite, 10g on ORE
heap.whelk: 8g on GO and ChEBI lite, 10g on ORE

settings.memory_cap: MemoryMax=12G and no swap per run
